name_story.story: Adama can be understood through the African form آدَمَا, whose central sense is adama; adam (west african form). Adama is the West African (Fulani/Hausa) form of the name Adam. It is used as a male given name.

faq.a: Adama is associated with the African form آدَمَا, whose core sense is adama; adam (west african form).

faq.q: What is the origin of Adama?
faq.a: Adama is associated with African. Adama is the West African (Fulani/Hausa) form of the name Adam. It is used as a male given name.
No — the underlying form is African, not Arabic.
Adama can occur in Muslim naming contexts, but it is better described as a African-origin name used within some Muslim naming traditions than as an exclusively Islamic religious term.
Adama should not be classified as a Quranic personal name without a direct Quranic basis. Adama is an African form of Adam, not a Quranic Arabic form.

faq.q: What does Adama mean in Urdu?
faq.a: In Urdu, Adama is rendered آدما and carries the sense آدما، حضرت آدم.

faq.q: What does Adama mean in Persian?
faq.a: In Persian, Adama is rendered آدما and carries the sense آدما، آدم.
A romanized syllable approximation is a-da-ma. No IPA transcription is asserted because a verified phonetic transcription was not available.

faq.q: What are the variants of Adama?
faq.a: Romanization variants include Adama, adama. Script forms are آدما, آدَمَا, आदमा.

faq.q: Is Adama a boy's or girl's name?
faq.a: Documented usage records this form as male. Gender is not inferred from the meaning of the word, and actual use may vary between communities.
